transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Well, what really pushed me to make this appointment is that I'm having a lot of trouble finishing things at work. I'm an auditor, and I keep starting these follow-up items after my audits, or after mentorship events, with every intention of getting them completely finished. 

But then, I don't know, I'll find out days later that the final email, or a review note, or the actual form never actually got done. I just leave things hanging without realizing it, and it's starting to become a real problem.
Did you experience similar difficulties with finishing tasks and staying organized when you were growing up in school, or is this a more recent issue?

No, it's definitely not a new thing. It's been happening since I was young. Even back in elementary school, my report cards always said that I was bright, but... well, that I lost assignments and rushed past small details. They also mentioned I talked out of turn and constantly needed reminders to finish my work. Actually, my mother still jokes about it. She always says I could easily ace a test, but then completely forget to turn in the project that was sitting right there in my backpack.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have an inner drive to always be on the go?

Yes, definitely. I always feel like I need to be doing something. Like, on weekends, I'll tell my husband that I'm just going to rest and take it easy. But... I just can't seem to actually do that. I end up bouncing around from putting in the laundry, to checking my emails, then maybe I'll go for a run, and then I'll start working on some volunteer planning. I just keep moving from one thing to the next, and I don't really stop until I'm completely exhausted.
